articles.summary: Seven individuals have been charged in a $110 million compound drug scheme involving Pharr Family Pharmacy (PFP). John Ageudo Rodriguez, the pharmacy owner, allegedly paid millions in kickbacks to marketers and physicians for referring prescriptions for high-reimbursing compound drugs that were often medically unnecessary. The scheme involved Dr. Mohammad Imtiaz Chowdhury paying kickbacks to his father Dr. Tajul Shams Chowdhury for prescription referrals, while clinic employees Araceli Gaona and Erika Hernandez Salinas facilitated the kickback payments. Marketers Mohammad Chowdhury, Alex Flores Jr., and Hector DeLaCruz served as conduits for the kickback scheme. From May 2014 to September 2016, PFP billed federal health care programs over $110 million with false and fraudulent claims. All seven defendants face charges including conspiracy to commit health care fraud, health care fraud, conspiracy to pay and receive illegal kickbacks, and conspiracy to commit money laundering.
